terminal.description: A shell in your workspace, already pointed at the offline lab model.

tasks.title: Catch the model cutting a summary short
tasks.description:
Before you change anything, prove what is happening. In `src/reproduce.ts`, implement `reproduceCutoff()`.

It should call the lab model directly with the same settings `summarizeComplaint` uses: `MODEL`, `MAX_TOKENS` and `buildMessages(longComplaint)`. Return an object with:

- `text`: the message content of the reply, unchanged
- `finishReason`: the `finish_reason` of that same reply

The check runs your function against the original `summarize.ts`.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.ts` and read the summary it prints.
Create a client with `new OpenAI()` and call `chat.completions.create` with the same options.
Return the content and the finish reason of the first choice.
Run the demo again and compare the two outputs.
hints: Every choice in a chat completion has more than a message. Print the whole first choice and look at its other fields.
You can import MODEL, MAX_TOKENS and buildMessages from summarize.ts, so your call matches the buggy one exactly.
The value you want is `res.choices[0].finish_reason`. For this complaint it should not say the model stopped on its own.

tasks.title: Never hand back a cut-off summary
tasks.description:
Fix `summarizeComplaint` in `src/summarize.ts` so the support team never sees half a summary.

Team policy for this endpoint:

- Check `finish_reason` on every reply.
- If the reply was cut off, ask again with double the `max_tokens` budget. Start at `MAX_TOKENS`.
- Make at most 3 requests in total.
- If the third reply is still cut off, throw an `Error` whose message contains `truncated`.
- Replies that finished normally are returned as they are.

Keep the function signature, including the optional `client` parameter.
nextSteps: Read the reply's `finish_reason` before returning the content.
Wrap the request in a loop that runs at most 3 times.
Double the budget after each cut-off reply.
Throw after the last attempt, then run `node src/demo.ts`.
hints: The bug is not the size of MAX_TOKENS. It is that the code never asks whether the reply is complete.
Keep the budget in a variable outside the loop so each attempt can use a larger one.
Inside the loop, return early when `finish_reason` is not 'length'. After the loop ends, the only thing left to do is throw.

tasks.title: Write the test that would have caught it
tasks.description:
Write vitest tests in `src/summarize.test.ts` that guard this bug for good. They should check that:

- a long complaint comes back as a complete summary, not one cut mid-sentence
- a complaint whose summary never fits makes `summarizeComplaint` reject with an error mentioning `truncated`

The check runs your test file three times: beside the original `summarize.ts` (it must fail), beside a correct fix (it must pass) and beside a fix that only raises `max_tokens` (it must fail). The fixtures in `src/complaints.ts` are there to help.
nextSteps: Write one test for the long complaint and one for the endless complaint.
Run `npx vitest run src/summarize.test.ts` against your fixed code.
Ask yourself what a version that only raises the limit would still get wrong.
hints: Look at a full summary from the lab model. What does its last character tell you?
For the error case, `await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(...)` lets you assert on the message.
A larger limit fixes the long complaint but not the endless one. Your second test is the one that catches that fix.
